title: Exchange of the trace-class sources: the kernel of the coefficient pushforward
statement:
Let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward diagram of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] (no Cartesian leg square, no properness
over $s$), with the notation and admissibility of
[def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. Then the kernel class of the coefficient
pushforward $[f,g]_!u$ is the transported kernel class of $u$:

$$
[\,[f,g]_!u\,]_P
=\rho_f\circ Rq_*[u]_P\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g
\quad:\ Rb_!A_D\longrightarrow P_Y ,
$$

where $\eta_g:A_D\to Rg_*A_C$ is the unit.

proof.text: Work at the finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$ already fixed by the two statement dependencies. Put $Z_X=X\times_sX$, $Z_Y=Y\times_sY$, $q=f\times f$, and use their projections $p_i,p'_i$. Thus $p'_iq=fp_i$ and $bg=qc$. Retain $Rc_!$ and $Rb_!$ throughout. Proper coincidence is used only for $f,g,q$. Write $K'=Rf_*K$, $V=D_XK$, $V'=Rf_*V$, $P_X=K\boxtimes V$, and $P_Y=K'\boxtimes D_YK'$. The finite-stage stability theorem puts $K',V',p_2^*K,p_1^!K$ and all the displayed tensor and internal-Hom objects in $D^b_{ctf}$; the same applies on $Y$. The exceptional adjoints needed for $p_i,p'_i,c,b,a_X,a_Y$ are available by exceptional admissibility for separated finite-type morphisms. Set $H_X=R\mathcal Hom(p_2^*K,p_1^!K)$ and $H_Y=R\mathcal Hom(p'^*_2K',p'^!_1K')$. The specified Künneth–Verdier maps are isomorphisms $\kappa_X:P_X\xrightarrow{\sim}H_X$ and $\kappa_Y:P_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}H_Y$. For exceptional compositions we use the constructible adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility], the composite Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and its transport under [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. In this normalization the counit of a composite is the outer counit after the direct image of the inner counit. This is a substitution in the composite-adjunction formula, not an application of the stronger ambient admissibility condition in clause (2) of [fix-prop-adjunctions]. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] (ii), each bounded constructible finite-stage input just listed is of etale origin. Thus the compact-support composition comparisons used below are the specified comparisons of the two statement definitions on their etale-origin domains, as collected in clause (3) of [prop-functor-package]. In particular the comparisons defining $\Xi$ and $\Xi_1$ are available on these inputs without an additional hypothesis on $K$.

For any correspondence $v:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$, the correspondence-class bijection sends $[v]:Rc_!A_C\to H_X$ to $v$. Its inverse is obtained by taking the tensor–Hom mate $A_C\to\mathcal H_c(K)$, using the canonical exceptional internal-Hom exchange to obtain a map $A_C\to c^!H_X$, and applying $Rc_!\dashv c^!$. The external-duality comparison is this exchange followed by $c^!\kappa_X^{-1}$, compatibly with evaluation and the same exceptional adjunction. Naturality of this Hom bijection therefore gives $[v]_P=\kappa_X^{-1}\circ[v]$. For $w:b_2^*K'\to b_1^!K'$, its tensor–Hom mate $A_D\to\mathcal H_b(K')$ corresponds under exceptional Hom exchange to a map $A_D\to b^!H_Y$ whose exceptional adjunct is $[w]$. Composing this mate with $b^!\kappa_Y^{-1}$ has exceptional adjunct $\kappa_Y^{-1}\circ[w]$, by naturality in the target of the exceptional Hom bijection; this is the defining mate of $[w]_P$. Thus $[w]_P=\kappa_Y^{-1}\circ[w]$. In particular no comparison with a differently normalized duality isomorphism is being assumed.

Let $\delta_1:Rq_*p_1^!K\to p'^!_1K'$ be the exceptional transpose of
$$Rp'_{1!}Rq_*p_1^!K\simeq Rf_!Rp_{1!}p_1^!K\xrightarrow{Rf_!\varepsilon_{p_1}}K'.$$
Define $\Phi:Rq_*H_X\to H_Y$ by its tensor–Hom transpose
$$Rq_*H_X\otimes p'^*_2K'\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_q}Rq_*(H_X\otimes p_2^*f^*K')\xrightarrow{Rq_*(1\otimes p_2^*\varepsilon_f)}Rq_*(H_X\otimes p_2^*K)\xrightarrow{Rq_*\mathrm{ev}}Rq_*p_1^!K\xrightarrow{\delta_1}p'^!_1K'.$$
All identifications here are composition comparisons. In particular $\delta_1$ is defined by a counit for the commuting square $p'_1q=fp_1$, with no base-change assertion for a leg square.

source.place: Step 1: definition of the transport map

proof.text:
For $t:Rb_!A_D\to H_Y$, denote by $B_b(t):Rb_{1!}b_2^*K'\to K'$ its image under the correspondence-class bijection followed by $Rb_{1!}\dashv b_1^!$. Explicitly, first identify the source with $Rp'_{1!}Rb_!b^*p'^*_2K'$, apply $\mathrm{PF}_b^{-1}$, then $Rp'_{1!}(t\otimes1)$, evaluation, and $\varepsilon_{p'_1}$. The composition and exceptional-adjunction comparisons give $b^!p'^!_1=b_1^!$, so $B_b$ is a bijection. Set $v^\flat=\varepsilon_{c_1}\circ Rc_{1!}v$. For $w=\delta\circ Rg_*v\circ\gamma$, naturality of the exceptional counit and the defining transpose of $\delta$ give
$$B_b([w])=Rf_!(v^\flat)\circ\Xi_1\circ Rb_{1!}\gamma.$$
This follows by replacing $\varepsilon_{b_1}\circ Rb_{1!}\delta$ by its defining composite $Rf_!\varepsilon_{c_1}\circ\Xi_1$ and moving $Rg_*v$ through the natural isomorphism $\Xi_1$.

Put $L=b_2^*K'$. The projection formula for the proper $g$ obeys
$$\mathrm{PF}_{g,A_C,L}\circ(\eta_{g,A_D}\otimes1_L)=\eta_{g,L}:L\longrightarrow Rg_*g^*L,$$
with the unit-object identifications understood. Indeed the ordinary transpose of the left side is $\varepsilon_{g,A_C}\circ g^*\eta_{g,A_D}\otimes1_{g^*L}=1_{g^*L}$ by the triangle identity; the transpose of the right side is also $1_{g^*L}$. Apply the explicit formula for $B_b$ to $\Phi\circ Rq_*[v]\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g$. Projection-formula compatibility with composition, for $bg=qc$, replaces the formulas for $b,q,c$ by the one for this composite. The displayed unit calculation turns the initial factor into $\eta_{g,L}$. The defining transpose of $\delta_1$ replaces its subsequent counit by $Rf_!\varepsilon_{p_1}$, and the definition of $[v]$ turns its evaluation into $v^\flat$. The resulting composite is exactly
$$Rb_{1!}L\xrightarrow{Rb_{1!}\eta_{g,L}}Rb_{1!}Rg_*g^*L=Rb_{1!}Rg_*c_2^*f^*K'\xrightarrow{Rb_{1!}Rg_*c_2^*\varepsilon_f}Rb_{1!}Rg_*c_2^*K\xrightarrow{\Xi_1}Rf_!Rc_{1!}c_2^*K\xrightarrow{Rf_!v^\flat}K'.$$
The first two arrows are $Rb_{1!}\gamma$ by definition. The bijectivity of $B_b$ and the preceding step prove
$$[\delta\circ Rg_*v\circ\gamma]=\Phi\circ Rq_*[v]\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g.\tag{b}$$

source.place: Step 2: the right-hand adjoint in (b), including the unit/projection calculation

proof.text:
Record explicitly the normalization of the proper product comparison. For objects $M,N$ on $X$, let $\Theta_{M,N}=\mathrm{Ku}_!(f,f;M,N)^{-1}:Rf_*M\boxtimes Rf_*N\to Rq_*(M\boxtimes N)$. Its ordinary $q^*\dashv Rq_*$ transpose is
$$q^*(Rf_*M\boxtimes Rf_*N)=p_1^*f^*Rf_*M\otimes p_2^*f^*Rf_*N\xrightarrow{p_1^*\varepsilon_{f,M}\otimes p_2^*\varepsilon_{f,N}}p_1^*M\otimes p_2^*N.$$
To see this from the specified map, expand the inverse relative-product comparison into its two projection maps and the exchange map for the Cartesian product square. Transposing the exchange gives the pulled-back counit, and transposing each proper projection map gives $\varepsilon\otimes1$, by their defining formulas. Naturality moves the two counits to their respective factors; the intervening unit/counit pairs cancel by the two triangle identities. This leaves exactly the displayed tensor of counits. In particular $\Pi_f=\Theta_{K,V}$. Compatibility of these product comparisons with symmetry, iterated products, base change and projection formula is supplied by the relative-product coherence lemma; it will be used below with the actual geometric operations, which satisfy the stated six-functor identities. More explicitly, the projection compatibility used below is obtained from clause (ii) with a third entry $\operatorname{id}_B$ carrying the coefficient object $L$ on $B$: the two bracketings agree, and clause (iv), $\kappa_{f,\operatorname{id}}(K,L)=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^{-1}$, identifies their identity-factor product maps with the inverse projection formulas. This gives the commuting product/projection diagram used in step 10.

source.place: Step 3: normalization of the product comparison entering (a)

proof.text:
Let $e_X:V\otimes K\to\omega_X$ be evaluation and $t_X:Ra_{X!}\omega_X\to A_s$ the structural exceptional counit. Write $J_X(W):Rp_{1!}(K\boxtimes W)\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes a_X^*Ra_{X!}W$ for $\mathrm{Ku}_!(\operatorname{id}_X,a_X)$. The tensor–Hom and exceptional transpose of $\kappa_X$ is the map
$$C_X:Rp_{1!}(P_X\otimes p_2^*K)=Rp_{1!}(K\boxtimes(V\otimes K))\xrightarrow{J_X(V\otimes K)}K\otimes a_X^*Ra_{X!}(V\otimes K)\xrightarrow{1\otimes a_X^*Ra_{X!}e_X}K\otimes a_X^*Ra_{X!}\omega_X\xrightarrow{1\otimes a_X^*t_X}K.$$
This is a direct substitution in the definition: $\beta$ transposes the two evaluations, and $\alpha_{\operatorname{id},a_X}$ transposes the product comparison followed by the exceptional counit. Explicitly, putting $e_Y:D_YK'\otimes K'\to\omega_Y$, $t_Y:Ra_{Y!}\omega_Y\to A_s$, and $J_Y(U)=\mathrm{Ku}_!(\operatorname{id}_Y,a_Y;K',U)$, the transpose on $Y$ is
$$C_Y=(1_{K'}\otimes a_Y^*t_Y)\circ(1_{K'}\otimes a_Y^*Ra_{Y!}e_Y)\circ J_Y(D_YK'\otimes K').$$
Indeed the tensor transpose of $\beta$ is $1_{K'}\boxtimes e_Y$, while the exceptional transpose of $\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_Y,a_Y}$ is $(1_{K'}\boxtimes t_Y)\circ\mathrm{Ku}_!$; naturality of $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ composes these into the displayed formula. All regroupings use the specified tensor symmetry, including its Koszul signs.

source.place: Step 3: the evaluation transpose of the specified Künneth–Verdier map

proof.text:
We compare $\kappa_Y\rho_f$ and $\Phi Rq_*\kappa_X$ after tensor–Hom and exceptional adjunction, with common source $T=Rp'_{1!}(Rq_*P_X\otimes p'^*_2K')$. Put $W=V\otimes f^*K'$. Define $Q:T\to K'\otimes a_Y^*Ra_{X!}W$ by this specified sequence: apply $\mathrm{PF}_q$ under $Rp'_{1!}$; use $p'_1q=fp_1$ to obtain $Rf_!Rp_{1!}(K\boxtimes W)$; apply $Rf_!J_X(W)$; then apply $\mathrm{PF}_f^{-1}$ to $Rf_!(K\otimes f^*a_Y^*Ra_{X!}W)$. Here $a_X=a_Yf$. Define $d:Ra_{X!}W\to A_s$ by
$$Ra_{X!}(V\otimes f^*K')\xrightarrow{Ra_{X!}(1\otimes\varepsilon_f)}Ra_{X!}(V\otimes K)\xrightarrow{Ra_{X!}e_X}Ra_{X!}\omega_X\xrightarrow{t_X}A_s.$$
By the definition of $\Phi$, naturality of the projection formulas, and the formula for $C_X$, the transpose of $\Phi Rq_*\kappa_X$ is $(1_{K'}\otimes a_Y^*d)\circ Q$: the final $\delta_1$ and $\varepsilon_{p'_1}$ are precisely $Rf_!\varepsilon_{p_1}$, as established by its defining transpose.

source.place: Step 3: an explicit common transpose for the right side of (a)

proof.text:
The transpose of $\kappa_Y\rho_f$ is the same composite. Substitute $\rho_f=(1\boxtimes\chi_f)\Pi_f^{-1}$ and the displayed formula for $C_Y$. Before evaluation this gives the map
$$T\longrightarrow K'\otimes a_Y^*Ra_{Y!}(V'\otimes K')$$
obtained by $\Pi_f^{-1}$ and $J_Y(V'\otimes K')$. Apply $1\otimes a_Y^*Ra_{Y!}\operatorname{PF}_{f,V,K'}$ and use $Ra_{Y!}Rf_!=Ra_{X!}$. Put $U=Y\times_sX$, $r=f\times\operatorname{id}_X$, $h=\operatorname{id}_Y\times f$, and $\pi=\operatorname{id}_Y\times a_X$, so $q=hr$, $p'_1h=\pi$, and $\pi r=fp_1$.

source.place: Step 3: beginning of the common-transpose comparison

proof.text:
Define $E_r(W)=\operatorname{Ku}_!(f,\operatorname{id}_X;K,W)$ and $J_{Y,X}(W)=\operatorname{Ku}_!(\operatorname{id}_Y,a_X;K',W)$. After applying $Rp'_{1!}\operatorname{PF}_q$ to $T$, the product/projection comparison of [lem-trf-product-projection-comparison] identifies both routes with
$$R\pi_!Rr_!(K\boxtimes W)\xrightarrow{R\pi_!E_r(W)}R\pi_!(K'\boxtimes W)\xrightarrow{J_{Y,X}(W)}K'\otimes a_Y^*Ra_{X!}W.$$
This uses the relative-product coherence with the third identity factor carrying $p'^*_2K'$, together with exchange pasting and the canonical compact-support composition comparisons.

source.place: Step 3: product/projection route through the mixed product

proof.text:
For the route defining $Q$, the mixed-product route lemma [lem-trf-mixed-product-route-comparison] gives, after $R\pi_!Rr_!=Rf_!Rp_{1!}$,
$$J_{Y,X}(W)\circ R\pi_!E_r(W)=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,a_Y^*Ra_{X!}W}^{-1}\circ Rf_!J_X(W).$$
Thus the intermediate route is exactly $Q$ as defined in step 8; no evaluation or dual-pushforward compatibility is used in this identification.

source.place: Step 3: identification of the intermediate route $Q$

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-dual-pushforward-evaluation-counit] with $M=V=D_XK$. It gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{K'}\circ(\chi_f\otimes1)=\tau_f\circ Rf_*e_X\circ\mu_{f,V,K},\qquad
\mu_{f,V,K}=Rf_*(1_V\otimes\varepsilon_f)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{f,V,K'}.$$
Thus the remaining evaluation, after the projection map already introduced in step 9, is obtained by applying the ordinary counit to the second factor, then $e_X$, then $\tau_f$.

Finally, the composite-adjunction counit formula, transported along the conjugate composition comparison specified by constructible admissibility, gives
$$t_Y\circ Ra_{Y!}\tau_f=t_X.$$
Here $\tau_f$ uses the canonical isomorphism $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$ of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition], which is the component at $A_s$ of the conjugate comparison in [def-trf-admissibility]. This is [lem-trf-dualizing-counit-transitivity].

The two transpose calculations now have the same composite: the product part is the map $Q$, the evaluation part is $1_{K'}\otimes a_Y^*d$, and the structural counit is $t_X$. Hence the transposes of $\kappa_Y\rho_f$ and $\Phi Rq_*\kappa_X$ coincide. Bijectivity of the tensor--Hom and exceptional adjunction bijections proves
$$\kappa_Y\circ\rho_f=\Phi\circ Rq_*\kappa_X.\tag{a}$$

Take $v=u$ in (b) and use the coefficient-pushforward definition. Step 2 gives $[u]=\kappa_X[u]_P$ and $[[f,g]_!u]_P=\kappa_Y^{-1}[[f,g]_!u]$. Substitution followed by (a) gives
$$[[f,g]_!u]_P=\kappa_Y^{-1}\Phi\,Rq_*\kappa_X\,Rq_*[u]_P\,\Xi\,Rb_!\eta_g=\rho_f\,Rq_*[u]_P\,\Xi\,Rb_!\eta_g.$$
The domain is $Rb_!A_D$ and the codomain is $P_Y$, as asserted. The proof used only the two commuting leg relations; the Cartesian squares in the relative-product construction are product squares, not leg squares.
